gates.title: A release-shaped commit still carries a working, in-sync vendored engine wheel for both agent skills, standalone and offline
gates.invariant: Every new feature, adapter or catalog adds or extends a build gate in `verification/`

rubric.pass: a throwaway release-shaped commit built by force-adding the gitignored vendored wheel and lock for both skills actually carries them in its git tree, with no tracked file (such as pyproject.toml) left drifted and uncommitted; extracting each skill folder from that commit alone and running its S-10 self-test passes standalone, offline, with no sibling engines/ checkout; the committed wheel matches a fresh build of that commit's own engines/python byte for byte; a release commit with a missing, corrupted or stale wheel turns the check red; `--release` on a named branch refuses and commits nothing; a wheel and lock committed onto a branch turn the standing checks red, while a release commit no branch contains passes them
rubric.fail: the release-shaped commit never advances past HEAD or is missing the wheel/lock from its tree, a skill's standalone self-test fails or needs the network, the committed wheel does not match a fresh build of its own engines/python, or the self-test's six seeded faults (missing, corrupted, stale, drifted pyproject.toml, release cut on a named branch, wheel committed onto a branch) fail to turn the check red

faults.description: the release-shape check stops invoking the real release step and runs only the plain wheel build instead, so the release-shaped tree it builds never actually lands the wheel and lock in a tagged tree
the standing checks stop asserting that no branch commit tracks a vendored wheel or lock, so a wheel committed onto main or a phase branch by hand would pass CI
the standing check treats every commit as a release commit no branch contains, so a wheel and lock committed onto a branch are excused

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command and read the FAIL lines; tools/skill_release_shape_check.py builds the release-shaped commit and runs the standalone install, tools/vendor_skill_engine.py builds and checks the wheel itself, and skills/README.md 'Install and pin (S-10)' documents the release procedure this gate proves.

gates.title: Every tracked uv.lock resolving cryptography still resolves a real Intel-macOS wheel (ADR-0024)
gates.invariant: Every new feature, adapter or catalog adds or extends a build gate in `verification/`

rubric.pass: every tracked uv.lock that names cryptography (engines/python and adapters/supply-chain, which pin the platform-marker split directly, plus every other workspace that resolves it transitively through the editable agent-conformance dependency) resolves at least one cryptography wheel tagged macosx_*_universal2 or macosx_*_x86_64, so a fresh install on an Intel Mac never falls back to a source build; the check's own self-test proves its matcher discriminates a lock with such a wheel from one that resolves only Linux/Windows/arm64 wheels
rubric.fail: any tracked lock naming cryptography resolves no Intel-macOS wheel (a later version bump dropped the platform split, or a new workspace's lock was never generated against the split pyproject.toml), or the self-test's seeded fault (the matcher always reporting no problem) fails to turn the check red

faults.description: the matcher stops checking lock text for an Intel-macOS wheel and always reports no problem, so a later cryptography bump that drops the platform split in any tracked lock would pass silently

gates.fix_hint: Run the gate's command and read the FAIL lines; tools/cryptography_intel_wheel_check.py names each offending uv.lock, which needs `uv lock` run inside it once its editable agent-conformance dependency (engines/python/pyproject.toml, ADR-0024) carries the platform split again.

gates.title: The otel-genai adapter's translation layer (bytes -> canonical AgentCE events) is byte-identical across Python, TypeScript, and Java over all 9 vendor fixtures plus all 18 hostile vectors
gates.invariant: Evaluator modules carry determinism tests (order, locale, and clock independence) and golden files.

rubric.pass: tools/otel_genai_adapter_check.py's --self-test confirms every vector matches Python's own reference and the comparator discriminates the truncation/enum-filter fault class, then the real cross-engine run over fresh builds of the TypeScript dist/ and the Java runnable jar produces byte-identical EVENT/REPORT/ERROR output in all three engines for all 25 vectors
rubric.fail: any vector's output disagrees between python, typescript, or java, or the self-test's comparator fails to discriminate the seeded truncation/enum-filter fault

faults.description: TypeScript: the tool-protocol enum filter is dropped from the otel-genai port, so an out-of-enum gen_ai.tool.protocol value passes through unfiltered into the mapped ToolCall payload instead of being silently dropped, which the truncation-and-enums vector's cross-engine comparison catches

gates.fix_hint: run verification/gates/otel_genai_parity.sh and read the MISMATCH lines, each naming the vector and the two engines that disagree; the reference implementation is engines/python/agentce/records/otel_genai.py, ported in engines/typescript/src/otelGenai.ts and engines/java/src/main/java/org/agentce/OtelGenai.java.
